lines.text: Earns 18% a year on all the money it uses
lines.why: For every ₹100 of shareholders' money and loans in the business, it made ₹18 of operating profit last year (better than 64% of Auto & auto components). Past years: steady; recent trend improving. Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 15, weak < 10 (default rule, all sectors).

lines.text: Keeps ₹12 of every ₹100 of sales as operating profit
lines.why: Operating margin 12.3% (better than 62% of Auto & auto components). Past years: steady; recent trend flat. Colour from close peers (Automobile and Auto Components, 39 stocks): middle half 8.39–16.1 (band rule PROXY).
For every ₹100 of shareholders' money, it has borrowed ₹31 (better than 44% of Auto & auto components). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≤ 0.5, weak > 1 (default rule, all sectors).

For every ₹100 of reported profit in recent years, ₹82 actually came in as cash (better than 14% of Auto & auto components). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 0.8, weak < 0.5 (default rule, all sectors).
₹100 of sales 3 years ago is about ₹212 now (better than 97% of Auto & auto components). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 10, weak < 0 (default rule, all sectors).

lines.text: Profit per share growing 39% a year
lines.why: ₹10 of earnings per share 3 years ago is about ₹27.0 now (better than 89% of Auto & auto components). Colour from the sector rule (PROXY): good ≥ 10, weak < 0 (default rule, all sectors).

valuation.text: Price tag: in line with its close peers
valuation.why: The whole business costs 24× its yearly operating cash profit (EBITDA). Colour from close peers (Automobile and Auto Components, 37 stocks): middle half 13.4–26.0 (band rule PROXY).

lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.
lenses.vd: In Benjamin Graham's spirit: would see a mixed picture (2 checks use fewer years than the rule needs).

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore
ch.w: Graham avoided small companies; ₹5,000 crore is our Indian translation of 'adequate size'.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2
ch.w: For every ₹100 it owes within a year, it holds ₹158 of cash, stock and dues coming in.

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹170 cr vs working capital ₹633 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years
ch.r: Positive earnings in each of the last 10 years
ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see; the earlier years are not in the free data.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: A gap of about 70 months without a dividend (2016-11 to 2022-09).

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years (3-year averages at each end)
ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved +122%.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings
ch.w: You pay ₹64 for every ₹1 of average yearly profit over the last 3 yrs.
You pay ₹6.82 for every ₹1 of net worth.

ch.r: Price < √(22.5 × EPS × book value per share)
ch.w: With EPS ₹21.6 and book value ₹150 per share, Graham's ceiling price is ₹270.

lenses.st: Wonderful business at a fair price
lenses.sp: Wants a simple business with a lasting edge, high returns without debt, and trustworthy managers.
lenses.vd: In Warren Buffett's spirit: would see a mixed picture (2 checks use fewer years than the rule needs).

ch.r: Could you explain how it makes money in two sentences?
q: What does it sell, and to whom?
Will people still need this in 10 years?

ch.r: A lasting edge: brand, low cost, network or switching costs
q: Why can't a well-funded rival copy it?
Has it kept high returns through bad years?

ch.r: ROE ≥ 15% in at least 8 of the last 10 years, with debt-to-equity < 0.5
ch.w: More than 2 weak years already.

ch.r: No loss in 10 years
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see.

ch.n: Doesn't eat its cash in capex
ch.r: Capex < 50% of operating cash flow (5-year sum)
ch.v: Capex was 127% of cash from operations over 4 yrs
ch.w: Of every ₹100 of cash the business brought in, ₹127 went back into plant and equipment.

ch.r: Share count up no more than 5% over the years we have
ch.w: Your slice of the company hasn't been shrunk by new share issues.

ch.r: Candid, sensible with capital, no governance red flags
ch.v: No management red flags in our automatic checks (checked: auditor changes, CFO/KMP changes, credit ratings, SEBI orders, promoter holding, pledge).
ch.w: Our automatic checks are a starting point only.
q: Do they admit mistakes in the annual report letter?
Have past acquisitions and capex paid off?

ch.n: Bought with a margin of safety
ch.r: Price ≥ 25% below estimated intrinsic value
ch.w: Needs the fair-value (DCF) estimate, which arrives in Stage 4.

ch.r: Promoters own ≥ 25% and have pledged none

ch.r: Share count not higher than last year

ch.r: Sales ÷ assets higher than last year
